confidence_notes: I based the restaurant, coffee and beer anchors on web searches of aggregated cost-of-living data. These were Numbeo figures from June 2026 as cited by Expatica: inexpensive meal about EUR 15.6, three-course meal for two about EUR 78, cappuccino about EUR 1.63, and 0.5 L domestic draft about EUR 5.2. Other aggregators gave similar numbers. I converted them at about 1.10 USD per EUR, which comes from RBA cross rates. I nudged them up slightly for July peak season. Crowdsourced figures vary, and beer varies the most between sources. I found no La Spezia-specific price for wine or cocktails. The cocktail figure assumes a local spritz costs EUR 6-8 and a mixed cocktail EUR 8-10, based on general Italian aperitivo benchmarks. The wine figure is set to roughly match the price of a draft beer. These two anchors are less certain. The four accommodation anchors are estimates from general knowledge only; I did not search for or check any listings. La Spezia is the main budget base for visiting the Cinque Terre, so July demand pushes prices up a lot. The town also has few registered hostels, so the hostel anchors are the least certain.
comparable_city_reasoning: I compared La Spezia with mid-sized Ligurian and Tuscan coastal cities such as Livorno and Genoa, adjusted upward for high July demand from Cinque Terre visitors. Restaurant prices are near the Italian mid-sized-city average. Summer accommodation costs are closer to those of popular Italian Riviera destinations.
